  "10.0.0.1"
  "72.255.233.2"
  "255.255.255.255"

Must not match:
  "255.139.8.007"
  "148.20.255"
  "0.0.255.1000"
  "256.1.1.1"

Reply with only the pattern in a ```regex fenced block.

items.prompt_text:
Write a Python regular expression that matches an IPv4 address: four decimal octets from 0 to 255 separated by dots, with no leading zeros (0 is fine, 01 is not), optionally followed by a CIDR prefix length: "/" and a number from 0 to 32 with no leading zeros.

It will be tested with re.fullmatch (so anchors are optional) against held-out strings: it must match every valid string and reject every invalid one. Examples (shown as JSON strings):

Must match:
  "0.253.0.45/26"
  "255.43.149.0"
  "255.0.34.111"
  "0.185.14.8"

Must not match:
  "255.32.16.1000"
  "01.234.95.46"
  "38.201.48.0."
  "256.1.1.1"

Reply with only the pattern in a ```regex fenced block.

Write a Python regular expression that matches an IPv4 address: four decimal octets from 0 to 255 separated by dots, with no leading zeros (0 is fine, 01 is not), followed by a required CIDR prefix length: "/" and a number from 0 to 32 with no leading zeros.

It will be tested with re.fullmatch (so anchors are optional) against held-out strings: it must match every valid string and reject every invalid one. Examples (shown as JSON strings):

Must match:
  "0.0.120.143/32"
  "255.255.255.0/26"
  "255.188.109.3/4"
  "235.255.59.0/24"

Must not match:
  "128.128.-1.0/24"
  "0.0.255.3"
  "5.11.90.154/33"
  "17.147.4.0/8/8"

Reply with only the pattern in a ```regex fenced block.
